legacy_conversion_note: Source: source/Y2/Session 2/Air Traffic Controller/ (Case Study_ Air Traffic Controller.docx + Guides Notes.docx + 3 embedded images + a duplicate O1fMt.png). KEPT AS THE ORIGINAL AUTHORS' OWN GIVEN FICTIONAL DATA (analogous to a-coachs-dilemma's box scores -- a word-problem's given numbers, not externally sourceable because the flight, airline flight number, and crew are invented): the fuel-leak table in Appendix E (all 9 readings, verbatim from the docx table), the aircraft data in Appendix F (66,500 kg takeoff weight, 139 passengers, 6,875 gal / 26,025 L tank, 4.88 gal/seat/hr standard burn, 542 mph/35,000 ft pre-failure and 418 mph/25,000 ft post-failure cruise), and the Appendix C cruise-performance table's specific cell values (could not be matched against a public Boeing FCOM excerpt -- proprietary documentation -- so NOT claimed as independently verified real data; flagged honestly in Appendix C's own text per MCS-21/T1-08 rather than claimed 'verbatim real'). RETUNED for the SPEC Section 2 balance test: the legacy docx states the aircraft's position as 'currently 943 miles northeast of OGG.' Recomputing this case's own fuel model (steady-state leak rate x distance, per Appendix E/F) at 943 mi produced remaining fuel of 2,205.7 gal for Option A vs 348.9 gal for Option B once the real great-circle distance from that position to SFO (1,444.8-1,757.9 mi depending on which reading of the flavor-text coordinates vs. the real OGG-SEA route bearing is used) is computed -- an 84%+ margin, far over SPEC Section 2's 20% cap, because a twin-engine trans-Pacific flight only 943 mi out of a ~2,600+ mi crossing is structurally much closer to turning back than to reaching any mainland point. Per SPEC Section 2 and case-write.md step 11 ('if the better option wins by more than ~20%, retune a constraint -- not by hiding data'), this scenario parameter was retuned from 943 mi to 1,200 mi (the position further along the same real OGG-SEA bearing where the two routes' fuel margins land close together by construction of the real geometry, not by adjusting the leak rate or tank capacity), producing the disclosed 5.55% margin recorded below. This is a scenario-parameter retune, not an invented fact -- 1,200 mi is presented in case.md the same way the original 943 mi was, as a given flight-tracking figure, with no external source needed for a fictional aircraft's fictional position. EXTERNALLY VERIFIED (real, current, cited in sources[]): OGG and SFO's real published coordinates (S1/S2), the great-circle/haversine distance method used to compute the 1,214 mi SFO-diversion distance from those coordinates (S3), Jet A fuel density used for the D5 weight computation (S4), a public corroborating range for 737-800 cruise KIAS/Mach (S5, since Appendix C's exact cell values could not be independently verified -- see above), and the real August 2015 Kilo/Ignacio/Jimena triple-hurricane event the Appendix D satellite photo depicts (S6) -- the image is real but the case's own storm ('Typhoon Ignacio,' September 2026) is fictional and differently dated, disclosed in the image caption. The legacy Guide Notes' Twist (organs aboard needing a same-night connection to Seattle, viable via SFO but not via OGG) is preserved in FACILITATOR.md, with the personal 'coach's own family member on the transplant list' sub-plot from the original dropped -- it added no math and read as unnecessary personal/family-hardship framing layered onto an already medically-weighted twist; the organs-in-transit stakes alone carry the same values-vs-numbers tension. A real, sourced fact (S7, heart transplant cold ischemic time) was added to give the Twist's urgency claim real grounding, kept facilitator-only since the Twist must not be pre-leaked in case.md. Appendix B's two 'suggested research topic' bullets replace the legacy docx's unlinked resource titles ('Article: Flying With Only One Engine', 'Mach vs. Airspeed vs. Altitude') -- the original gave no URLs, so these are kept as research prompts (matching Challenge 1's own 'research and find a resource' framing) rather than presented as citations. The legacy Appendix B (wind-vector world map, image2.png) was reviewed and excluded from case.md -- it is a generic global map with no Hawaii-specific data beyond what Appendix D's text wind report already states, and including it as a lettered appendix with no distinct referenced data would risk an orphan-appendix finding; the file itself is still saved to assets/ for reference.

modeling_assumptions.text: This case models the post-failure fuel-flow rate for the remainder of either route using the plateaued (steady-state) value from Appendix E's readings (5 m 05 s onward), rather than integrating the changing rate during the first five minutes after the failure -- because the pre-plateau window covers only a small fraction of either remaining route's total distance.

Fuel burned before the engine failure is modeled using the standard (two-engine) burn rate over the time the aircraft took to reach its current position at its pre-failure cruising speed -- the leak-rate table in Appendix E only begins at the moment of failure, so it does not apply to this earlier stretch of the flight.

For the Appendix C cruise-performance lookup (D5), this case uses the nearest table weight bracket at or below the computed current aircraft weight, at the current altitude -- a standard conservative convention for a quick manual table lookup, rather than a full linear interpolation between listed weight rows.

The aircraft's position and the distance-to-OGG figure are this case's own given scenario data (a fictional flight); the distance from that position to SFO is computed from it using the real great-circle method and SFO's real published coordinates (sources S1-S3), not independently sourced as a fact about a real flight.

deliverables.text: A steady-state fuel-flow rate: the mean of Appendix E's plateaued readings (5 m 05 s onward), rounded to one decimal place.
A total-fuel-burned calculation for Option A (return to OGG): pre-failure burn (Appendix F) plus D1's rate over the 1,200-mile return distance (Appendix A).
The same total-fuel-burned calculation for Option B (divert to SFO), using the 1,214-mile distance from the current position to SFO (Appendix A).
A side-by-side comparison table, in both gallons and liters, of the fuel remaining at touchdown for Option A vs. Option B.

A cruise-performance lookup: the aircraft's approximate current weight (starting weight minus the weight of fuel burned before the failure, Appendix F), used with the current altitude to look up recommended KIAS and fuel flow from Appendix C.

balance.argument_a: Returning to OGG is the shorter leg (1,200 mi vs. 1,214 mi), so at the same D1 steady-state leak rate (3.7 gal/mi) it burns less total fuel -- 5,941.8 gal vs. 5,993.6 gal for SFO -- and lands with more fuel in the tank: 933.2 gal (3,532.1 L, about 13.6% of the 6,875-gal tank) vs. 881.4 gal (3,335.9 L, about 12.8% of tank) for SFO, a 51.8-gallon, 5.6% margin once D2/D3's arithmetic is worked. It also avoids extending the flight, and any further risk of the leak worsening, over a longer route.
balance.argument_b: Diverting to SFO is clear weather the entire way (Appendix D), while returning to OGG means flying a hail-damaged, one-engine aircraft directly back into the same typhoon whose hail caused the failure in the first place. SFO's fuel margin at touchdown (881.4 gal, 3,335.9 L, about 12.8% of the 6,875-gal tank) is smaller than OGG's (933.2 gal, 13.6% of tank) by only 51.8 gal -- a 5.6% gap under this case's own numbers -- but it is still positive: the aircraft is not modeled as running out of fuel on either route, so the weather risk is real and uncontested by the fuel numbers, not merely a tiebreaker.
balance.margin_basis: Primary metric: gallons of fuel remaining in the tank at touchdown. Option A (OGG): 933.2 gal remaining. Option B (SFO): 881.4 gal remaining. Margin = |933.2-881.4|/933.2 = 5.55%, rounded 5.6% -- within SPEC Section 2's 20% cap, and close enough that the fuel-only comparison alone does not settle the case; see derived{} for the full worked figures.
balance.stability: WINNER stable, SURVIVABILITY not stable, under a +/-50% flex of the one real modeled assumption (MA1, steady-state leak rate 3.7 gal/mi -- see sensitivity_model.py). At -50% (1.85 gal/mi) both options land safely with a large margin (3,153.2 vs 3,127.3 gal, 0.82% gap). At +50% (5.55 gal/mi) BOTH options run the tank dry before landing (-1,286.8 and -1,364.5 gal); Option A is nominally 'less negative' but neither route is physically completable on the modeled fuel at that flex, so the resulting margin%% is a formula artifact (negative baseline), not a meaningful percentage -- same class of finding as this project's own Seton Hall zero-baseline note in skills/case-readiness/SKILL.md. Fully disclosed in FACILITATOR.md's Sensitivity note; not treated as an eliminated risk.

sensitivity_note: A safety-decision case (aviation emergency) with no illness/death content required by the base math -- the fuel comparison alone does not model any crash or death outcome (both options land with positive fuel remaining by construction). The Twist (facilitator-only, see FACILITATOR.md) introduces a medically-weighted stake (organ transplant urgency) -- flag per SPEC Section 6 for the discussion lead, and note the twist is deliberately framed around protecting/delivering organs for transplant (a 'doses delivered' framing), not around casualties or death. See sensitivity_model.py for the P5 assumption-flex result on the one real modeled assumption (the steady-state leak rate).

cohort_bands.note: Anchors 2-3 run as written; the room debates fuel-safety vs. weather-safety (the case's real two-axis tension) before the Twist adds the organ-transport time pressure -- expect the room to split roughly evenly on A vs B even before the Twist, since the fuel margin (5.6%) is close and the weather/engine-damage argument for B has real force independent of the numbers.
Anchors 2-3 combine into one pass; D1-D3's fuel-burn arithmetic is worked once as a shared example for Option A, then each pair completes Option B and D4-D5 independently.

No vote to take -- Anchor 1 becomes a stated initial position instead of a cold-call; guide plays devil's advocate directly, defending whichever option the Hero did NOT pick, focused specifically on the axis (fuel vs. weather) the Hero under-weighted.
